agentContributions.notes: Story requests Live Preview of Content in CMS — a novel capability not present in the codebase. The central integration point is useContent (236+ consumers), which any live-preview mechanism must plug into so that all existing Contentstack components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) reflect real-time content updates without per-component changes. Acceptance criteria are empty, so VCs are derived from the description alone. Contentstack services are unreachable at test time, so VCs are scoped to our side of the boundary — what our code receives, requests, and renders given a known response.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array, so all 14 ACs are new. I derived them from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the technical notes (useContent with 236+ consumers, ContentstackContext, ContentstackLink, contentCard), and openspec's own analysis noting that Contentstack services are unreachable at test time. ACs are scoped to our side of the boundary — what our code receives, processes, and renders. Key areas covered: (1) data flow through useContent (AC-1, AC-2), (2) fallback/disconnection behavior (AC-3, AC-4, AC-5), (3) XSS/security (AC-6), (4) accessibility (AC-7), (5) cross-site consistency (AC-8), (6) stale data prevention (AC-9, AC-14), (7) opt-in/production safety (AC-10), (8) performance (AC-11), (9) error handling for edge cases (AC-12, AC-13). CAVEAT: I did not have access to the file contents of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, ContentstackLink.tsx, or contentCard.ts — specific ACs around data shapes, existing error paths, or current context API surface may need adjustment once those files are reviewed.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: BLOCKER: The agent contributions reference files that do not exist in this repository. Specifically: useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, ContentstackLink.tsx, and contentCard.ts were all referenced by both openspec and speckit, but none are present. Searches for 'useContent', 'Contentstack', 'ContentstackContext', 'ContentstackLink', and 'contentCard' return zero matches across the entire repository. The repository contains only src/index.ts, src/spec-mode-runner.ts, orchestrations/prd.json, package.json, README.md, and tests/. Speckit itself noted it 'did not have access to the file contents' of these files — confirming no verification was performed. The '236+ consumers' claim for useContent is unverifiable and likely originates from a different project context. Both agents added non-overlapping value conceptually (openspec identified integration points and boundary-scoping; speckit derived 14 ACs covering data flow, fallback, security, accessibility, performance, and edge cases), but their work is built on file references that cannot be validated against this codebase. A writer sent to implement this story would be directed to edit files that do not exist. Human review required to either (a) confirm this story belongs to a different repository and should be processed there, or (b) provide the correct file paths that exist in this repository.
